extracted.intended_audience: Researchers considering applying for the SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship (prospective applicants / project leaders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal eligibility/evaluation rules for applicants to the SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship, including participation requirements, timelines, required documents, and procedural constraints for submission and grant management.

rubrics_metrics.name: General participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have a proven record of at least two years' research activity at a Swiss higher education research centre, or they must be Swiss nationals or have a Swiss higher education degree. They have never held a professorship position nor is such a position foreseen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Eccellenza Regulations to determine formal eligibility. This is an overarching eligibility filter — check full regulations for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher qualification and minimum research experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers: have a doctorate (PhD) or at least three years of research activity after obtaining their higher education degree (equivalent qualification to a doctorate); have acquired at least three years of research experience after their doctorate or equivalent qualification to a doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimum of three years' research work must be met by the submission deadline; no exceptions can be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission time window for researchers (academic age)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must submit their application up to eight years after their PhD defense or after the date of the equivalent qualification to a doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time periods are calculated on the basis of the relevant submission deadline for Eccellenza applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical researchers: medical qualification and experience requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers who do clinical work: have a medical exam (state examination or equivalent); have acquired at least three years of clinical work and at least 2 years of research activities after their medical exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical applicants must meet both the clinical-work and research-activity minimums and follow the extended timeline below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission time window for clinical researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers who do clinical work may submit their application up to 12 years after their medical exam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time periods are calculated from the submission deadline; consult the guidelines/forms to compute eligibility accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic age vs net academic age (definitions and use)
rubrics_metrics.description: The academic age indicates how much time has passed since the doctorate and is relevant for calculation of the time window in accordance with personal requirements. The net academic age indicates how much time you have been able to spend doing research since your doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Net academic age is taken into account in the evaluation (i.e., evaluators consider interruptions/reduced research time). Use the net academic age form to declare periods where research time was reduced or interrupted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: In the mobility statement you should give reasons for your choice of research institution and set out your completed and planned mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear justification for mobility choices and list completed/planned stays; this information informs reviewers about career development and fit of the institutional environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net academic age form content
rubrics_metrics.description: In the form used to calculate the net academic age, you should indicate how much time you have been able to spend doing research since your doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions in the relevant forms; document career interruptions, parental leave, clinical duties, or other factors that reduce research time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambizione grantee restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambizione grantees can apply for an SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship or a PRIMA grant 18 months after starting their Ambizione grant at the earliest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you currently hold an Ambizione grant, check start dates to ensure the 18-month minimum before applying is satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of resubmissions after rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose request for an SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship was rejected may submit one further application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single resubmission opportunity is permitted following rejection; plan revisions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No exceptions for the three-year research minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: No exceptions can be granted regarding the minimum of three years' research work required after the doctorate; this requirement needs to be met by the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect discretionary waivers for this requirement; ensure eligibility before preparing a full application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent SNSF project rule (parallel submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot submit an Eccellenza proposal if you have an SNSF project under evaluation. However, if you already have an approved or ongoing project under the project funding scheme when you submit your Eccellenza proposal, you may continue that project if its research topic is clearly different from that of the SNSF Eccellenza proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit while another SNSF application of yours is under evaluation. If holding an approved project, document clear topic separation between projects to avoid conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professorial-position prohibition (current/past/promised)
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers must not hold, have held, or have been assured of a temporary or permanent position as an assistant professor or professor in Switzerland or abroad at the time of the submission deadline and for the entire duration of the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positions that bar application are characterized by independent research and teaching duties not bound by instructions and the right to supervise doctoral theses. For applicants from abroad, comparable titles may differ — contact SNSF if in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via the mySNF platform. The mySNF platform will be opened for submission three months before the respective application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mySNF portal and consult the 'Guidelines for submitting an Eccellenza proposal' PDF; missing the platform opening window may prevent submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation procedure structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation procedure for Eccellenza comprises two stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed criteria for each stage are available in the Evaluation procedure document; applicants should consult the linked procedure to understand stage-specific requirements and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required institutional confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: A written confirmation of the higher education institution is a required document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain the institution's written confirmation in the required format (see downloadable PDF template) and include it with the application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary measures and support available
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary measures include mobility grants in projects, the Flexibility Grant, media training, and a gender equality grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider applying for or using these supplementary measures where appropriate; information and eligibility are provided in the Documents section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for transferring a grant to a new institution
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to transfer your grant to another institution, including the funds covering your salary, contact the SNSF explaining the reasons for the move as well as its added value for your project or your career. The new research institution must provide confirmation letters; an authorized body of the former research institution must acknowledge the change in writing to the SNSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNSF evaluates transfer requests considering project feasibility and relevance for the grantee's career; include required documents and justification in your written request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of taking a job outside academic research during the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: If you take on a new job outside of academic research, you must inform the SNSF accordingly. The SNSF terminates the grant and the remaining amount of the grant must be refunded to the SNSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify SNSF promptly of employment changes; anticipate grant termination and potential financial consequences for exiting academia during the grant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find core documents and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations, guidelines and other important information can be found under 'Documents' (Eccellenza Regulations, Guidelines for submitting an Eccellenza proposal, Guidelines for researchers who do clinical work, Written confirmation of the higher education institution, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Eccellenza Regulations and scheme-specific guidelines carefully to ensure compliance with formal requirements and to prepare application materials correctly.
